item.content:encoded: This would be more greater without the excessive sponge mints

I don't like expungements on this one. Overall they feel like "hmmm I dunno what to write. Expungement, I choose you!"; in the description, about the internal structure of the cables, you could use a redaction, which is way more fitting ("guys, I'm redacting this part 'cause it's techno-babble you don't need to know" over the "guys, I'm expunging this 'cause you mustn't know it but it's bad. oh so very bad."), while in containment procedures…no. Just no. In the logs…well, they may fit, but I'm unsure about that; and dude, Foundation personnel writing this stuff will always: (a) translate everything they put in, (b) expunge/redact what the readers shouldn't know, or (c) use a special secret code just for those meant to know. SCP articles are meant (my own interpretation) to be read by agents who could have something to do with the illustrated SCPs, and they are most certainly able to fluently read Morse code; why leaving it be? It's just losing precious time translating it, for the agents. I heavily suggest to either translate the beginning of the interview, or redact it. That said, I like the idea and the picture, and that gained my upvote, but…well, if someone refined the execution I'd like it better.
